source_records.abstract: Abstract Dengue fever (DF) is a mosquito-borne viral disease caused by four dengue virus serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4) and remains a major public health concern in tropical regions, including Indonesia. In 2024, Mataram City reported 364 confirmed dengue cases, indicating a substantial local burden. This observational cross-sectional study was conducted from November 2024 to January 2025 in eight high-incidence neighborhood associations within the Karang Pule Health Center working area, Mataram City. Mosquito larvae and ovitrap samples were collected from case-based households following WHO entomological surveillance guidelines, reared to F1 adult females, and pooled (20 mosquitoes per site) for viral RNA extraction. Dengue virus detection and serotyping were performed using a one-step RT-PCR assay with serotype-specific primers, including appropriate positive and negative controls to ensure assay validity. Five of eight sampling locations were positive for DENV. DENV-3 was the predominant serotype, detected in three locations, while co-circulation of DENV-2 and DENV-3 was identified in two locations. No DENV-1 or DENV-4 was detected. Villages such as West Pagutan exhibited the highest proportion of reported cases and incidence rates. Environmental parameters (temperature, humidity, water temperature, and light intensity) were recorded at each site and analyzed descriptively. The detection of DENV in F1-generation Aedes aegypti supports evidence of ongoing local viral circulation and suggests the potential contribution of vertical (transovarial) transmission in maintaining the virus reservoir. This study provides fine-scale, sub-district-level mapping of dengue serotype distribution in an urban Indonesian setting, offering localized evidence to support targeted vector control strategies while acknowledging limitations related to sample size and geographic coverage.

papers.title: Dengue virus serotype classification from complete genomes using a Transformer with chunk-based sequence modeling and explainability analysis
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used for genomic surveillance of infectious diseases, but predictive models must be evaluated under realistic generalization settings and interpreted cautiously. We present XAI-DENFormer, an explainability-oriented framework for dengue virus (DENV) serotype classification from complete viral genomes. A curated dataset of 29,091 publicly available DENV genomes was encoded as nucleotide-level one-hot sequences and processed with a chunk-based Transformer encoder designed for memory-efficient whole-genome analysis. Generalization was assessed using three complementary validation protocols: CD-HIT cluster-aware, geographical, and temporal validation. DENFormer variants were benchmarked against Logistic Regression, a feed-forward neural network, Longformer, and Performer under identical conditions. The mean-pooling DENFormer configuration maintained high performance across all three validation protocols, with accuracies of 98.68–99.91% across CD-HIT folds, 97.18–100.00% across geographical holdouts, and 96.35–99.86% across temporal holdouts. To inspect model behavior, we combined attention maps, Gradient × Input attributions, embedding visualizations, and regional statistical analyses. The resulting profiles supported distributed serotype-associated signals across structural, non-structural, and untranslated regions rather than reliance on a single genomic locus. XAI-DENFormer provides a robust and interpretable framework for large-scale DENV genome classification and model-guided genomic inspection.

We present XAI-DENFormer, an explainability-oriented framework for dengue virus (DENV) serotype classification from complete viral genomes. A curated dataset of 29,091 publicly available DENV genomes was encoded as nucleotide-level one-hot sequences and processed with a chunk-based Transformer encoder designed for memory-efficient whole-genome analysis. Generalization was assessed using three complementary validation protocols: CD-HIT cluster-aware, geographical, and temporal validation. DENFormer variants were benchmarked against Logistic Regression, a feed-forward neural network, Longformer, and Performer under identical conditions. The mean-pooling DENFormer configuration maintained high performance across all three validation protocols, with accuracies of 98.68–99.91% across CD-HIT folds, 97.18–100.00% across geographical holdouts, and 96.35–99.86% across temporal holdouts. To inspect model behavior, we combined attention maps, Gradient × Input attributions, embedding visualizations, and regional statistical analyses. The resulting profiles supported distributed serotype-associated signals across structural, non-structural, and untranslated regions rather than reliance on a single genomic locus. XAI-DENFormer provides a robust and interpretable framework for large-scale DENV genome classification and model-guided genomic inspection.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces XAI-DENFormer, a novel framework for dengue virus serotype classification using complete genomes. The research addresses the growing need for accurate and interpretable genomic surveillance tools by developing a Transformer-based model with chunk-based sequence modeling. The model was validated using three complementary protocols: CD-HIT cluster-aware, geographical, and temporal validation, achieving high accuracy across all settings. The mean-pooling configuration of DENFormer outperformed other models, with accuracies ranging from 96.35% to 99.91%. The framework's explainability features, including attention maps and embedding visualizations, revealed distributed serotype-associated signals across various genomic regions. These findings suggest that XAI-DENFormer can be a valuable tool for large-scale dengue virus classification and genomic analysis. However, the abstract-only evidence limits the depth of interpretation, and the study's results are presented with moderate confidence due to the lack of detailed experimental validation.

papers.title: Genomic analysis identifies candidate supergene architecture for host-feeding behavior in wild Aedes aegypti dengue vector mosquitoes
papers.abstract: Background Aedes aegypti is the primary arboviral vector globally, and its affinity to feed on human hosts is a key determinant of transmission intensity. Despite the epidemiological importance of anthropophily, the genomic architecture underlying the molecular basis of host-feeding behavior remains understudied. Methods Here, we present an integrated genome-wide association study (GWAS) and structural variant analysis of host-feeding behavior in 21 field-collected Ae. aegypti females phenotyped as human-blood-fed (HF; n = 11) or non-human-blood-fed (NHF; n = 10). Whole-genome sequencing yielded 661,519 high-quality SNPs distributed across all three chromosomes. Principal component analysis on a linkage disequilibrium-pruned dataset revealed modest population structure (PC1 = 11.69%, PC2 = 10.98%). Results GWAS using a general linear model with five PC covariates (λ = 1.05) identified 11 suggestive SNPs in genes including an actin binding protein on chromosome 2 and G-protein coupled receptor 39 on chromosome 3. Chromosomal inversion analysis using Delly identified an HF-specific inversion on chromosome 2 harboring 13 genes across three functionally coherent chemosensory categories: the sensory developmental regulator tap, odorant receptors (Or6, Or31, Or33) and an odorant-binding protein ( Gp68 ), and eight gustatory receptor genes ( Gr15–Gr19a, Gr35, Gr36, Gr66 ). Conclusion The concentration of co-adapted chemosensory genes within a single non-recombining chromosomal unit is consistent with a possible supergene model of anthropophily, paralleling inversion-mediated behavioral divergence in Anopheles gambiae . These exploratory findings provide a preliminary genomic framework for host-seeking behavior in Ae. aegypti and identify probable candidate loci warranting functional validation before application to vector surveillance.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景 埃及伊蚊是全球主要的虫媒病毒 媒介,其以人类 宿主 为食的亲和力是 传播 强度的关键决定因素。尽管人类性在流行病学上具有重要性,但 宿主 进食行为的分子基础的基因组结构仍未得到充分研究。方法在这里,我们提出了一项综合的 基因组 全关联研究 (GWAS) 和对 21 种现场采集的白蚊 宿主 摄食行为的结构变异分析。埃及伊蚊雌性的表型为人类血液喂养(HF;n = 11)或非人类血液喂养(NHF;n = 10)。全 基因组 测序产生了分布在所有三个染色体上的 661,519 个高质量 SNP。对连锁不平衡修剪数据集的主成分分析揭示了适度的群体结构(PC1 = 11.69%,PC2 = 10.98%)。结果 GWAS 使用具有 5 个 PC 协变量 (λ = 1.05) 的一般线性模型在基因中识别出 11 个暗示性 SNP,包括 2 号染色体上的肌动蛋白结合蛋白和 3 号染色体上的 G 蛋白偶联受体 39。使用 Delly 进行的染色体倒位分析确定了 2 号染色体上的 HF 特异性倒位,其中包含 13 个基因,涵盖三个功能上一致的化学感应类别:感觉发育调节器水龙头、气味受体(Or6、 Or31、Or33)和气味结合蛋白(Gp68)以及八个味觉受体基因(Gr15–Gr19a、Gr35、Gr36、Gr66)。结论 单个非重组染色体单位内共同适应的化学感应基因的浓度与可能的人性化超基因模型一致,与冈比亚按蚊中倒位介导的行为分歧相一致。这些探索性发现为伊蚊 宿主 寻找行为提供了初步的基因组框架。aegypti 并确定可能的候选基因座,在应用于 媒介 监测 之前保证功能验证。

papers.full_text: Received: June 15, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 685 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.35 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ Examining Dengue-related Information Diffusion on Indonesian Twitter Through Sentiment-based Network Analysis, Spatial Mapping, and Temporal Dynamics Ribka Devina Margaretha1 Wiwik Anggraeni1* 1Department of Information Systems, Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember, Surabaya, Indonesia * Corresponding author’s Email: wiwik@is.its.ac.id Abstract: Dengue fever remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, yet studies integrating sentiment analysis, Social Network Analysis, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on social media remain limited. This study proposes an integrated framework applied to 5,715 dengue-related tweets collected from Indonesian Twitter between January 2021 and December 2025. Sentiment classification using IndoBERT revealed a predominantly neutral discourse (65.23%), with meaningful negative (20.31%) and positive (14.45%) proportions. Sentiment-weighted interaction networks were constructed and analysed, revealing highly fragmented structures with modularity scores exceeding 0.98. Healthcare professionals emerged as the most robustly influential actors by betweenness centrality, with PageRank-based influence conditional on self-loop treatment, while the Ministry of Health held the highest in-degree values. Spatial analysis, based primarily on self-reported user locations, indicated geographic concentration along the Java-Bali corridor, and temporal analysis revealed recurring peaks in January and June aligned with Indonesia's wet season and dengue outbreak cycles. These findings demonstrate the value of integrating sentiment, network, and spatial dimensions for comprehensive public health communication analysis. Keywords: Dengue fever, Sentiment-based network analysis, Spatial analysis, Temporal analysis, Social media. 1. Introduction Dengue fever remains one of the fastest- spreading vector-borne diseases and a major global public health challenge, endemic in more than 100 countries and threatening approximately 3.9 billion people, particularly in Southeast Asia and Latin America [1-3]. In Indonesia, dengue is highly endemic and continues to cause serious health problems, with more than 257,000 reported cases and over 1,400 deaths in 2024 [4]. The increasing spread of dengue, driven by climate change, urbanisation, and population growth, has also heightened public concern regarding outbreaks and prevention efforts [5]. The growing use of social media, particularly Twitter, has created new opportunities to observe public responses and information exchange related to disease outbreaks[6-8]. Through mentions, replies, and reposts, Twitter enables rapid information diffusion across communities, while certain accounts play disproportionately influential roles in shaping discussions [9]. Social Network Analysis (SNA) has therefore been widely applied to identify influential actors and examine information diffusion dynamics within online networks [10, 11]. Beyond interaction patterns, social media discussions also reflect public opinions and emotional responses toward ongoing health issues [12]. Sentiment analysis provides a complementary approach for capturing these perceptions, and incorporating sentiment information into network analysis can deepen understanding of how dengue- related discussions propagate and evolve on social media [13]. Dengue burden and public health responses are not uniformly distributed across Indonesia, with substantial disparities observed across provinces and Received: June 15, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 686 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.35 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ regions due to differences in population density, climate conditions, healthcare accessibility, and vector control capacity [14, 15]. Public perceptions and responses to health information also vary across communities due to cultural and social differences [16]. These regional variations highlight the importance of incorporating spatial information to better understand geographic differences in dengue- related discussions, public sentiment, and information dissemination patterns. Previous studies have applied SNA to identify influential users and examine information diffusion in online discussions, while sentiment analysis has been widely used to understand public perceptions toward health-related issues, and spatial analysis has been employed to reveal geographic variations in dengue transmission and public health responses. However, these approaches are typically investigated in isolation, limiting a comprehensive understanding of how interaction structures, public sentiment, and geographic context collectively shape online discussions. Studies integrating sentiment-weighted social networks with spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on Indonesian Twitter remain particularly limited, highlighting the need for a more integrated analytical framework. To address this gap, this study integrates sentiment analysis, SNA, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related Twitter discussions, constructing sentiment-weighted interaction networks and analysing them alongside geographic and temporal dimensions. The specific contributions of this study are: • Analysis of the spatial distribution of discussions and sentiments across Indonesian cities • Construction of sentiment-based interaction networks capturing both communication structure and public perception • Identification of national-level influential users using PageRank, degree centrality, and betweenness centrality • Identification of regional influential users across multiple Indonesian cities • Analysis of temporal discussion patterns and sentiment dynamics • Visualisation of interaction networks illustrating information diffusion structures. The remainder of this paper is structured as follows. Section 2 reviews related literature. Section 3 describes the data and methodology. Section 4 presents the results and discussion. Section 5 summarises the findings and outlines future directions. 2. Related works 2.1 Social network analysis for information diffusion SNA has been widely applied to investigate information diffusion and interaction patterns in online social networks, modelling users as nodes and interactions as edges to identify influential actors and community structures [17]. Various approaches have been proposed for influencer detection, including the NetDegree centrality measure and the Weighted Correlated Influence (WCI) model combining user activity and network topology [18, 19]. SNA has also been applied to explore community structures and communication dynamics in domain-specific discussions [20]. In health-related contexts, SNA has been used to identify key influencers, dominant topics, and communication structures shaping public awareness [10, 11, 21]. However, most existing health-related SNA studies focus on network topology and influencer identification without incorporating sentiment context or geographic variation. Bonifazi et al. identified influential users in COVID-19 vaccine Twitter discourse through a multilayer network approach, but did not construct sentiment-segmented networks or examine geographic distributions [21]. Durmaz and Hengirmen applied SNA to vaccine- related Twitter discourse in Turkey using in-degree and betweenness centrality, but did not integrate sentiment labels or examine spatial distributions [22]. Pratiwi et al. combined SNA and sentiment analysis for asthma-related Twitter discourse, but did not link findings to geographic distributions or construct sentiment-segmented networks [10]. The absence of sentiment integration and spatial context in these studies limits the depth of understanding achievable in health-related discourse analysis. 2.2 Sentiment analysis in social media discussions Sentiment analysis is widely applied to understand public opinions in social media, with recent studies demonstrating the effectiveness of advanced language models including IndoBERT for Indonesian-language content [23, 24]. Ishfaq et al. and Eliacik and Erdogan have incorporated sentiment into network-based analyses for influential user identification [25, 26]. However, applications combining sentiment and network characteristics in health-related discussions remain limited. Dengue-specific sentiment studies such as Abdul Ghani et al. demonstrate the value of sentiment for disease surveillance but do not Received: June 15, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 687 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.35 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ construct interaction networks or link findings to geographic distributions [27]. Indonesian-language classification studies such as Supriyadi and Makatita and Nabiilah et al. demonstrate strong model performance without connecting findings to network structures or spatial patterns [23, 24]. While Ishfaq et al. and Eliacik and Erdogan incorporate sentiment into network analyses, neither examined dengue- related discourse or linked findings to spatial distributions [25, 26]. No prior study has simultaneously applied sentiment-integrated SNA to dengue-related Indonesian Twitter data, leaving a gap in understanding how emotional responses and interaction structures collectively shape dengue information diffusion. 2.3 Spatial analysis in health-related studies Spatial analysis has gained increasing attention in public health and social media research for understanding geographic variations in behaviour and information dissemination. Lovera and Cardinale demonstrated that geolocation enriches the interpretation of social media discussions [34]. Similarly, Wu et al. highlighted the value of geospatial enrichment for understanding large-scale sentiment behaviour[35]. In health-related contexts, Lin et al. revealed linguistic and geographic disparities in COVID-19 public awareness through social media, while Zhang et al. applied geographical and temporal analysis to health-related tweets to identify spatiotemporal disease discussion patterns at regional level [36, 37]. However, these studies focus on geographic distribution patterns without modelling user interaction networks or identifying regional-level influential users. Lin et al., Zhang et al., Lovera and Cardinale, and Wu et al. all incorporate geolocation into social media analysis, but do not construct interaction networks, identify influential users, or examine how sentiment varies across network communities [z-37]. Studies applying spatial analysis to dengue-related social media discourse, such as Abdul Ghani et al., have similarly focused on geographic mapping without modelling user interaction dynamics or examining sentiment- segmented network structures [27]. The absence of interaction network modelling and sentiment integration limits understanding of how network dynamics and public sentiment collectively shape dengue information diffusion. 2.4 Research gap Despite the established contributions of SNA, sentiment analysis, and spatial analysis individually, existing health-related social media studies address these dimensions in isolation, as demonstrated across Sections 2.1 to 2.3, focusing on network topology without sentiment context [10, 21, 22], applying sentiment classification without network or spatial linkage[23, 27], or examining geographic patterns without modelling interaction dynamics [34-37]. While sentiment analysis and network approaches have each been applied to health-related social media discourse individually, their simultaneous integration with spatial analysis in the specific context of dengue-related Indonesian Twitter data remains unexplored. No prior study has proposed a unified framework simultaneously capturing the structural, emotional, and geographic dimensions of dengue-related information diffusion on Indonesian Twitter. This study addresses that gap by integrating sentiment analysis, SNA, and spatial analysis within a single framework, constructing sentiment- segmented interaction networks to examine how different emotional contexts shape network structure and influencer profiles, mapping discussion distributions and regional influencer patterns across Indonesian cities, and tracing temporal dynamics of both discussion volume and sentiment evolution over a five-year period. This integrated approach offers a more complete understanding of information dissemination patterns, influential users, and public perceptions across different locations and time periods than prior single-method studies have provided. 3. Materials and method 3.1 Dataset Dengue-related tweets were collected from Twitter (X) between January 2021 and December 2025 using the Scweet Python library with three keywords: "dbd" (dengue haemorrhagic fever acronym in Indonesian), "Aedes aegypti" (the dengue-carrying mosquito species), and "demam berdarah dengue" (dengue haemorrhagic fever). Data collection was conducted between 9-14 April 2026. The collected tweets span the period from January 2021 to December 2025, reflecting the full range of historical tweets retrievable through Scweet at the time of collection; Scweet retrieves historical tweets via browser automation rather than the official Twitter/X API, and collection completeness is therefore subject to the platform's search indexing and any rate-limiting constraints encountered during scraping. Collection was conducted as a series of discrete scraping sessions per keyword and sub-period, with no session returning a tweet count at or exceeding the configured retrieval limit (500-1,000 tweets, depending on keyword), indicating retrieval without truncation within each queried window. A completeness check was performed by examining the year-by-year distribution of collected tweets to confirm the absence of anomalous gaps or artificially uniform collection patterns; as detailed in Section 4.6.1, tweet volume varied organically across the five-year period, consistent with externally documented dengue activity patterns in Indonesia rather than indicating systematic data loss. Each tweet record contains textual content, publication date, user information, engagement statistics, and interaction attributes including mentions, replies, and reposts. The collected dataset serves as the primary source for all sentiment, network, spatial, and temporal analyses conducted in this study. 3.2 Method This study employs an integrated analytical framework consisting of data preprocessing, sentiment classification, network construction, community detection, spatial analysis, and temporal analysis. Data preprocessing The datasets collected from different periods were combined and filtered to retain only the attributes required for analysis, including tweet identifiers, usernames, tweet content, timestamps, language information, location attributes, and interaction metadata. User mentions and replies were extracted separately to support network construction. Duplicate tweets and records with missing values in essential attributes were removed, and tweet texts were cleaned through lowercasing, URL removal, mention and hashtag removal, number and punctuation removal, and whitespace normalisation. Location texts were normalised and matched against a reference dataset of Indonesian cities, with common aliases and abbreviations standardised to improve matching accuracy. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ Examining Dengue-related Information Diffusion on Indonesian Twitter Through Sentiment-based Network Analysis, Spatial Mapping, and Temporal Dynamics Ribka Devina Margaretha1 Wiwik Anggraeni1* 1Department of Information Systems, Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember, Surabaya, Indonesia * Corresponding author’s Email: wiwik@is.its.ac.id Abstract: Dengue fever remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, yet studies integrating sentiment analysis, Social Network Analysis, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on social media remain limited. This study proposes an integrated framework applied to 5,715 dengue-related tweets collected from Indonesian Twitter between January 2021 and December 2025. Sentiment classification using IndoBERT revealed a predominantly neutral discourse (65.23%), with meaningful negative (20.31%) and positive (14.45%) proportions. Sentiment-weighted interaction networks were constructed and analysed, revealing highly fragmented structures with modularity scores exceeding 0.98. Healthcare professionals emerged as the most robustly influential actors by betweenness centrality, with PageRank-based influence conditional on self-loop treatment, while the Ministry of Health held the highest in-degree values. Spatial analysis, based primarily on self-reported user locations, indicated geographic concentration along the Java-Bali corridor, and temporal analysis revealed recurring peaks in January and June aligned with Indonesia's wet season and dengue outbreak cycles. These findings demonstrate the value of integrating sentiment, network, and spatial dimensions for comprehensive public health communication analysis. Keywords: Dengue fever, Sentiment-based network analysis, Spatial analysis, Temporal analysis, Social media. 1. Introduction Dengue fever remains one of the fastest- spreading vector-borne diseases and a major global public health challenge, endemic in more than 100 countries and threatening approximately 3.9 billion people, particularly in Southeast Asia and Latin America [1-3]. In Indonesia, dengue is highly endemic and continues to cause serious health problems, with more than 257,000 reported cases and over 1,400 deaths in 2024 [4]. The increasing spread of dengue, driven by climate change, urbanisation, and population growth, has also heightened public concern regarding outbreaks and prevention efforts [5]. The growing use of social media, particularly Twitter, has created new opportunities to observe public responses and information exchange related to disease outbreaks[6-8]. Through mentions, replies, and reposts, Twitter enables rapid information diffusion across communities, while certain accounts play disproportionately influential roles in shaping discussions [9]. Social Network Analysis (SNA) has therefore been widely applied to identify influential actors and examine information diffusion dynamics within online networks [10, 11]. Beyond interaction patterns, social media discussions also reflect public opinions and emotional responses toward ongoing health issues [12]. Sentiment analysis provides a complementary approach for capturing these perceptions, and incorporating sentiment information into network analysis can deepen understanding of how dengue- related discussions propagate and evolve on social media [13]. Dengue burden and public health responses are not uniformly distributed across Indonesia, with substantial disparities observed across provinces and Received: June 15, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 686 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.35 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ regions due to differences in population density, climate conditions, healthcare accessibility, and vector control capacity [14, 15]. Public perceptions and responses to health information also vary across communities due to cultural and social differences [16]. These regional variations highlight the importance of incorporating spatial information to better understand geographic differences in dengue- related discussions, public sentiment, and information dissemination patterns. Previous studies have applied SNA to identify influential users and examine information diffusion in online discussions, while sentiment analysis has been widely used to understand public perceptions toward health-related issues, and spatial analysis has been employed to reveal geographic variations in dengue transmission and public health responses. However, these approaches are typically investigated in isolation, limiting a comprehensive understanding of how interaction structures, public sentiment, and geographic context collectively shape online discussions. Studies integrating sentiment-weighted social networks with spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on Indonesian Twitter remain particularly limited, highlighting the need for a more integrated analytical framework. To address this gap, this study integrates sentiment analysis, SNA, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related Twitter discussions, constructing sentiment-weighted interaction networks and analysing them alongside geographic and temporal dimensions. The specific contributions of this study are: • Analysis of the spatial distribution of discussions and sentiments across Indonesian cities • Construction of sentiment-based interaction networks capturing both communication structure and public perception • Identification of national-level influential users using PageRank, degree centrality, and betweenness centrality • Identification of regional influential users across multiple Indonesian cities • Analysis of temporal discussion patterns and sentiment dynamics • Visualisation of interaction networks illustrating information diffusion structures. The remainder of this paper is structured as follows. Section 2 reviews related literature. Section 3 describes the data and methodology. Section 4 presents the results and discussion. Section 5 summarises the findings and outlines future directions. 2. Related works 2.1 Social network analysis for information diffusion SNA has been widely applied to investigate information diffusion and interaction patterns in online social networks, modelling users as nodes and interactions as edges to identify influential actors and community structures [17]. Various approaches have been proposed for influencer detection, including the NetDegree centrality measure and the Weighted Correlated Influence (WCI) model combining user activity and network topology [18, 19]. SNA has also been applied to explore community structures and communication dynamics in domain-specific discussions [20]. In health-related contexts, SNA has been used to identify key influencers, dominant topics, and communication structures shaping public awareness [10, 11, 21]. However, most existing health-related SNA studies focus on network topology and influencer identification without incorporating sentiment context or geographic variation. elements_zh.methods: 登革热 仍然是印度尼西亚的一项重大公共卫生挑战,但整合情感分析、社交网络分析和空间分析来检查社交媒体上登革热相关信息传播的研究仍然有限。这项研究提出了一个综合框架,应用于 2021 年 1 月至 2025 年 12 月期间从印度尼西亚 Twitter 收集的 5,715 条登革热相关推文。使用 IndoBERT 进行的情感分类显示,主要是中性话语 (65.23%),有意义的负面言论(20.31%) 和正 (14.45%) 比例。构建和建立了情感加权交互网络,揭示了高度碎片化的结构,模块化得分超过 0.98。医疗保健专业人员通过介数中心性成为最具影响力的参与者,基于 PageRank 的影响力以自循环 治疗 为条件,而卫生部拥有最高的入度值。空间分析,主要基于用户自我报告位置、表明爪哇-巴厘岛走廊沿线的地理集中度以及时间分析显示 1 月和 6 月反复出现的高峰与印度尼西亚的雨季和登革热 暴发 周期一致。这些发现证明了整合情绪、网络和空间维度对于全面公共卫生传播分析的价值。

papers.title_zh: 通过基于情感的网络分析、空间映射和时间动态检查印度尼西亚 Twitter 上与登革热相关的信息传播
papers.source_body_en: Dengue fever remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, yet studies integrating sentiment analysis, Social Network Analysis, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on social media remain limited.This study proposes an integrated framework applied to 5,715 dengue-related tweets collected from Indonesian Twitter between January 2021 and December 2025.Sentiment classification using IndoBERT revealed a predominantly neutral discourse (65.23%), with meaningful negative (20.31%) and positive (14.45%) proportions.Sentiment-weighted interaction networks were constructed and analysed, revealing highly fragmented structures with modularity scores exceeding 0.98.Healthcare professionals emerged as the most robustly influential actors by betweenness centrality, with PageRank-based influence conditional on self-loop treatment, while the Ministry of Health held the highest in-degree values.Spatial analysis, based primarily on self-reported user locations, indicated geographic concentration along the Java-Bali corridor, and temporal analysis revealed recurring peaks in January and June aligned with Indonesia's wet season and dengue outbreak cycles.These findings demonstrate the value of integrating sentiment, network, and spatial dimensions for comprehensive public health communication analysis.
papers.abstract_zh: 登革热 仍然是印度尼西亚的一项重大公共卫生挑战,但整合情感分析、社交网络分析和空间分析来检查社交媒体上登革热相关信息传播的研究仍然有限。这项研究提出了一个综合框架,应用于 2021 年 1 月至 2025 年 12 月期间从印度尼西亚 Twitter 收集的 5,715 条登革热相关推文。使用 IndoBERT 进行的情感分类显示,主要是中性话语 (65.23%),有意义的负面言论(20.31%) 和正 (14.45%) 比例。构建和建立了情感加权交互网络,揭示了高度碎片化的结构,模块化得分超过 0.98。医疗保健专业人员通过介数中心性成为最具影响力的参与者,基于 PageRank 的影响力以自循环 治疗 为条件,而卫生部拥有最高的入度值。空间分析,主要基于用户自我报告位置、表明爪哇-巴厘岛走廊沿线的地理集中度以及时间分析显示 1 月和 6 月反复出现的高峰与印度尼西亚的雨季和登革热 暴发 周期一致。这些发现证明了整合情绪、网络和空间维度对于全面公共卫生传播分析的价值。

papers.title: A structural bridge between dengue virus tandem xrRNAs facilitates coordination of exonuclease resistance
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Orthoflavivirus RNA genomes resist host 5′–3′ exoribonucleases to produce subgenomic flaviviral RNAs (sfRNAs). This resistance is conferred by exoribonuclease-resistant RNA (xrRNA) structures within the viral 3′ untranslated region that often occur in tandem, and whose function can be coupled. In dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV2), this coupling results in changing patterns of sfRNA identity and abundance associated with the ability of the virus to adapt to host vs. The physical basis of this coupling was unknown. Using a combination of virology, biochemistry, bioinformatics, structural biology, and biophysics, we explored the structural and sequence determinants of tandem xrRNA coupling in DENV2. We discovered that the spatial proximity, order, and structural integrity of the tandem xrRNAs are all important for coupling. Furthermore, an unpaired A-rich linker that lies between the two xrRNAs is essential in stabilizing a specific structure that correlates to coupling. This A-rich sequence likely forms tertiary contacts with an adjacent stem-loop structure to form a physical bridge between the two xrRNAs, a finding that is supported by a mid-resolution cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) map of the DENV2 tandem xrRNAs. Disruption of the structure of this bridge by mutation changes the relative orientation or spacing between the tandem xrRNAs, which is correlated to their functional coupling. These findings help provide an explanation for the coupling between tandem xrRNAs, suggesting a new mechanistic hypothesis in which the two tandem xrRNAs can simultaneously encounter Xrn1. IMPORTANCE Dengue virus (DENV) generates non-coding subgenomic flaviviral RNAs (sfRNAs) that affect several cellular pathways and are important for successful infection. These sfRNAs are formed by structured RNA elements in the viral genome called exoribonuclease-resistant RNAs (xrRNAs), which fold into a distinct three-dimensional topology to block degradation by host cell exoribonucleases and often occur in tandem. Specific patterns of sfRNAs made during infection are important for host vs. vector fitness, and in DENV2, this pattern depends on functional coupling between tandem xrRNAs. However, the source of this functional coupling was unknown. We determined that an unpaired A-rich linker between the tandem xrRNAs is necessary for creating a structural bridge between the tandem xrRNAs. This bridge appears to favor a specific orientation between the tandem xrRNAs that is correlated to coupling and therefore to the patterns and relative abundance of sfRNAs produced during infection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue virus generates subgenomic flaviviral RNAs (sfRNAs) that are important for successful infection, but the mechanism underlying the functional coupling between tandem xrRNAs was unknown. This study aimed to uncover the structural basis of this coupling.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV2) and explored the structural and sequence determinants of tandem xrRNA coupling using a combination of virology, biochemistry, bioinformatics, structural biology, and biophysics. The research was conducted in a laboratory setting.
analysis.methods: The researchers used a multidisciplinary approach, combining virology, biochemistry, bioinformatics, structural biology, and biophysics to investigate the structural and sequence determinants of tandem xrRNA coupling in DENV2. They analyzed the spatial proximity, order, and structural integrity of the tandem xrRNAs and examined the role of an unpaired A-rich linker.
analysis.main_results: The study found that the spatial proximity, order, and structural integrity of the tandem xrRNAs are important for their coupling. Additionally, an unpaired A-rich linker between the two xrRNAs is essential for stabilizing a specific structure that correlates with coupling.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the A-rich linker forms a physical bridge between the tandem xrRNAs, favoring a specific orientation that is correlated with their functional coupling. This provides a new mechanistic hypothesis for how tandem xrRNAs can simultaneously encounter Xrn1.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results contribute to understanding the molecular mechanisms of dengue virus RNA resistance to host exoribonucleases, which could inform future studies on viral adaptation and the development of antiviral strategies targeting RNA degradation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only evidence, which limits the depth of analysis. However, the findings are supported by a mid-resolution cryo-EM map and mutation experiments, providing moderate confidence in the structural model proposed.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the structural basis of functional coupling between tandem xrRNAs in dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV2). The researchers used a multidisciplinary approach to explore how spatial proximity, order, and structural integrity of these xrRNAs contribute to their coupling. They discovered that an unpaired A-rich linker between the xrRNAs is essential for stabilizing a specific structure that correlates with functional coupling. The findings suggest that this A-rich linker forms a physical bridge between the xrRNAs, favoring a specific orientation that allows them to simultaneously encounter Xrn1. These results provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms of DENV2 RNA resistance to host exoribonucleases, which could inform future research on viral adaptation and antiviral strategies. The study is based on abstract-only evidence, which limits the depth of analysis, but the findings are supported by a mid-resolution cryo-EM map and mutation experiments, offering moderate confidence in the proposed structural model.

papers.title_zh: 登革病毒串联xrRNA之间的结构桥促进外切核酸酶抗性的协调
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Orthoflavivirus RNA genomes resist host 5′–3′ exoribonucleases to produce subgenomic flaviviral RNAs (sfRNAs). This resistance is conferred by exoribonuclease-resistant RNA (xrRNA) structures within the viral 3′ untranslated region that often occur in tandem, and whose function can be coupled. In dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV2), this coupling results in changing patterns of sfRNA identity and abundance associated with the ability of the virus to adapt to host vs. The physical basis of this coupling was unknown. Using a combination of virology, biochemistry, bioinformatics, structural biology, and biophysics, we explored the structural and sequence determinants of tandem xrRNA coupling in DENV2. We discovered that the spatial proximity, order, and structural integrity of the tandem xrRNAs are all important for coupling. Furthermore, an unpaired A-rich linker that lies between the two xrRNAs is essential in stabilizing a specific structure that correlates to coupling. This A-rich sequence likely forms tertiary contacts with an adjacent stem-loop structure to form a physical bridge between the two xrRNAs, a finding that is supported by a mid-resolution cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) map of the DENV2 tandem xrRNAs. Disruption of the structure of this bridge by mutation changes the relative orientation or spacing between the tandem xrRNAs, which is correlated to their functional coupling. These findings help provide an explanation for the coupling between tandem xrRNAs, suggesting a new mechanistic hypothesis in which the two tandem xrRNAs can simultaneously encounter Xrn1. IMPORTANCE Dengue virus (DENV) generates non-coding subgenomic flaviviral RNAs (sfRNAs) that affect several cellular pathways and are important for successful infection. These sfRNAs are formed by structured RNA elements in the viral genome called exoribonuclease-resistant RNAs (xrRNAs), which fold into a distinct three-dimensional topology to block degradation by host cell exoribonucleases and often occur in tandem. Specific patterns of sfRNAs made during infection are important for host vs. vector fitness, and in DENV2, this pattern depends on functional coupling between tandem xrRNAs. However, the source of this functional coupling was unknown. We determined that an unpaired A-rich linker between the tandem xrRNAs is necessary for creating a structural bridge between the tandem xrRNAs. This bridge appears to favor a specific orientation between the tandem xrRNAs that is correlated to coupling and therefore to the patterns and relative abundance of sfRNAs produced during infection.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 正黄病毒 RNA 基因组 可抵抗 宿主 5'–3' 核糖核酸外切酶,产生亚基因组黄病毒 RNA (sfRNA)。这种抵抗力是由病毒 3' 非翻译区内的外核糖核酸酶抗性 RNA (xrRNA) 结构赋予的,这些结构通常串联出现,并且其功能可以耦合。在 登革病毒 血清型 2 (DENV2) 中,这种偶联导致与病毒适应 宿主 的能力相关的 sfRNA 特性和丰度模式发生变化。这种偶联的物理基础尚不清楚。我们结合病毒学、生物化学、生物信息学、结构生物学和生物物理学,探索了 DENV2 中串联 xrRNA 偶联的结构和序列决定因素。我们发现串联 xrRNA 的空间邻近性、顺序和结构完整性对于偶联都很重要。此外,位于两个 xrRNA 之间的未配对的富含 A 的接头对于稳定与偶联相关的特定结构至关重要。这种富含 A 的序列可能与相邻的茎环结构形成三级接触,从而在两个 xrRNA 之间形成物理桥,这一发现得到了 DENV2 串联 xrRNA 的中分辨率冷冻电子显微镜 (cryo-EM) 图的支持。突变 破坏该桥的结构会改变串联 xrRNA 之间的相对方向或间距,这与其功能耦合相关。这些发现有助于为串联 xrRNA 之间的耦合提供解释,提出一种新的机制假设,其中两个串联 xrRNA 可以同时遇到 Xrn1。重要性 登革病毒 (DENV) 产生非编码亚基因组黄病毒 RNA (sfRNA),影响多种细胞途径,对于成功感染非常重要。这些 sfRNA 由病毒 基因组 中称为核糖核酸外切酶抗性 RNA (xrRNA) 的结构化 RNA 元件形成,它们折叠成独特的三维拓扑结构,以阻止 宿主 细胞核糖核酸外切酶的降解,并且通常串联发生。感染期间产生的 sfRNA 的特定模式对于 宿主 与 媒介 的适应性非常重要,并且在 DENV2 中,这种模式取决于串联 xrRNA 之间的功能耦合。然而,这种功能耦合的来源尚不清楚。我们确定串联 xrRNA 之间未配对的富含 A 的接头对于在串联 xrRNA 之间创建结构桥是必要的。这种桥似乎有利于串联 xrRNA 之间的特定方向,该方向与耦合相关,因此与感染期间产生的 sfRNA 的模式和相对丰度相关。

papers.title: Optimizing dengue virus surveillance in wastewater through shedding dynamics and RNA stability analysis: Implications for early warning systems
papers.abstract: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) for dengue virus (DENV) is a promising tool but hindered by a lack of fundamental data on viral shedding and stability. Here, we mapped high-resolution longitudinal shedding trajectories by analyzing 769 serial saliva, urine, and fecal specimens collected from a prospective cohort of 132 hospitalized patients across a 23-day post-symptom onset window, resolved degradation constants within authentic environmental matrices, and constructed a predictive forward sensitivity model. Clinical screening identified urine as the most reliable surveillance target, exhibiting a diagnostic positivity rate of 88.4%. However, stability experiments benchmarking a 25°C subterranean sewer baseline revealed that DENV-1 RNA within authentic patient excreta mixtures (mixed urine, feces, and saliva) degraded nearly fivefold faster than standard pseudovirus spikes in simplified controls, yielding a 90% decay time T 90 ) of approximately 3.4 days. Modeling results indicate that this accelerated degradation limits conventional centralized grab sampling to a detection threshold of 1 infection per 184 individuals. In contrast, near-source passive sampling can overcome this bottleneck, achieving a theoretical detection limit of 1 case per 35,130 people. Factoring in empirical field detection limits, this time-integrated approach maintains a highly sensitive practical detection threshold ranging from 1 case per 3,513 to 17,565 individuals.

Here, we mapped high-resolution longitudinal shedding trajectories by analyzing 769 serial saliva, urine, and fecal specimens collected from a prospective cohort of 132 hospitalized patients across a 23-day post-symptom onset window, resolved degradation constants within authentic environmental matrices, and constructed a predictive forward sensitivity model. Clinical screening identified urine as the most reliable surveillance target, exhibiting a diagnostic positivity rate of 88.4%. However, stability experiments benchmarking a 25°C subterranean sewer baseline revealed that DENV-1 RNA within authentic patient excreta mixtures (mixed urine, feces, and saliva) degraded nearly fivefold faster than standard pseudovirus spikes in simplified controls, yielding a 90% decay time T 90 ) of approximately 3.4 days. Modeling results indicate that this accelerated degradation limits conventional centralized grab sampling to a detection threshold of 1 infection per 184 individuals. In contrast, near-source passive sampling can overcome this bottleneck, achieving a theoretical detection limit of 1 case per 35,130 people. Factoring in empirical field detection limits, this time-integrated approach maintains a highly sensitive practical detection threshold ranging from 1 case per 3,513 to 17,565 individuals.

papers.title: Decompressive hemicraniectomy for fulminant acute disseminated encephalomyelitis following dengue fever: Case report and literature review
papers.abstract: Background: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) is a rare immune-mediated demyelinating disorder of the central nervous system that typically occurs after viral or bacterial infections. Although most patients respond favorably to immunomodulatory therapy, a small subset develops fulminant ADEM characterized by malignant cerebral edema, refractory intracranial hypertension, and a high risk of mortality. Decompressive craniectomy has rarely been reported as a life-saving intervention in such cases. Case Description: A 25-year-old woman developed fulminant ADEM following dengue fever and initially presented with recurrent seizures progressing to status epilepticus. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated extensive bilateral demyelinating lesions involving the frontoparietal, occipital, temporal, and cerebellar white matter, with extension into the corpus callosum. Despite aggressive medical management, including high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone, osmotherapy, sedation, and plasma exchange, the patient experienced progressive neurological deterioration associated with diffuse cerebral edema, anisocoria, and radiological evidence of impending cerebral herniation. Owing to the failure of maximal medical therapy, a left decompressive hemicraniectomy was performed. The patient subsequently underwent additional immunomodulatory treatment, survived the acute phase of the disease, and demonstrated significant neurological recovery. A review of the literature identified nine previously reported cases of fulminant ADEM treated with decompressive craniectomy. Conclusion: Fulminant ADEM is an uncommon but potentially fatal neurological emergency. In cases complicated by malignant cerebral edema and refractory intracranial hypertension, decompressive craniectomy may represent a life-saving therapeutic option. Early recognition and timely surgical intervention appear to be associated with favorable neurological outcomes.

papers.title_original: Decompressive hemicraniectomy for fulminant acute disseminated encephalomyelitis following dengue fever: Case report and literature review

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the use of decompressive hemicraniectomy for fulminant acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) following dengue fever. The central question is whether decompressive craniectomy is a viable life-saving intervention in cases of fulminant ADEM caused by dengue virus.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a case report combined with a literature review. It includes a single case study of a 25-year-old woman with fulminant ADEM following dengue fever and references nine previously reported cases of fulminant ADEM treated with decompressive craniectomy. The review does not explicitly report on meta-analysis or consensus processes.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that fulminant ADEM is an uncommon but potentially fatal neurological emergency. It suggests that decompressive craniectomy may represent a life-saving therapeutic option in cases complicated by malignant cerebral edema and refractory intracranial hypertension. Early recognition and timely surgical intervention are associated with favorable neurological outcomes.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence is limited to case reports, which are not robust enough to establish a definitive consensus. There is no mention of randomized controlled trials or large-scale studies to support the use of decompressive craniectomy in fulminant ADEM. The review also does not address the mechanisms underlying the development of fulminant ADEM or its relationship with dengue virus.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of decompressive craniectomy in fulminant ADEM caused by dengue virus. This includes conducting randomized controlled trials and exploring the pathophysiological mechanisms of fulminant ADEM. In clinical practice, early recognition of fulminant ADEM and prompt surgical intervention may be critical for improving patient outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the use of decompressive hemicraniectomy as a potential life-saving intervention for fulminant acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) following dengue fever. It presents a case report of a 25-year-old woman who developed fulminant ADEM after dengue infection and was treated with decompressive craniectomy. The review also summarizes nine previously reported cases of fulminant ADEM treated with similar interventions. The findings suggest that decompressive craniectomy may be a therapeutic option in severe cases of ADEM with malignant cerebral edema and refractory intracranial hypertension. However, the evidence is limited to case reports, and there is a need for more rigorous studies to confirm its efficacy. The review highlights the importance of early recognition and timely surgical intervention in improving outcomes for patients with fulminant ADEM.

papers.title_zh: 登革热后的暴发性急性播散性脑脊髓炎的去骨瓣减压术:病例报告及文献综述
papers.source_body_en: Background: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) is a rare immune-mediated demyelinating disorder of the central nervous system that typically occurs after viral or bacterial infections. Although most patients respond favorably to immunomodulatory therapy, a small subset develops fulminant ADEM characterized by malignant cerebral edema, refractory intracranial hypertension, and a high risk of mortality. Decompressive craniectomy has rarely been reported as a life-saving intervention in such cases. Case Description: A 25-year-old woman developed fulminant ADEM following dengue fever and initially presented with recurrent seizures progressing to status epilepticus. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated extensive bilateral demyelinating lesions involving the frontoparietal, occipital, temporal, and cerebellar white matter, with extension into the corpus callosum. Despite aggressive medical management, including high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone, osmotherapy, sedation, and plasma exchange, the patient experienced progressive neurological deterioration associated with diffuse cerebral edema, anisocoria, and radiological evidence of impending cerebral herniation. Owing to the failure of maximal medical therapy, a left decompressive hemicraniectomy was performed. The patient subsequently underwent additional immunomodulatory treatment, survived the acute phase of the disease, and demonstrated significant neurological recovery. A review of the literature identified nine previously reported cases of fulminant ADEM treated with decompressive craniectomy. Conclusion: Fulminant ADEM is an uncommon but potentially fatal neurological emergency. In cases complicated by malignant cerebral edema and refractory intracranial hypertension, decompressive craniectomy may represent a life-saving therapeutic option. Early recognition and timely surgical intervention appear to be associated with favorable neurological outcomes.

papers.title: Targeting Dengue Viral Proteins with Eco-Friendly Nanotechnology: A Promising Path for Antiviral Research
papers.abstract: Dengue virus (DENV), a mosquito-borne pathogen belonging to the Flaviviridae family, continues to be a major global public health concern, causing millions of infections annually across tropical and subtropical regions. The virus encodes both structural and non-structural proteins that play critical roles in its replication, assembly, and immune evasion. Despite substantial research progress, there is still no specific antiviral drug available, and current treatment remains primarily supportive. This review highlights the significance of DENV structural proteins (C, prM/M, and E) and non-structural proteins (NS1–NS5) as potential molecular targets for antiviral interventions. Green-synthesized silver, gold, and iron oxide nanoparticles have demonstrated strong inhibitory activity against DENV by targeting key viral proteins such as the envelope (E), NS3 protease/helicase, and NS5 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. These nanoparticles interfere with viral entry, replication, and protein synthesis while exhibiting high biocompatibility and minimal cytotoxicity. Collectively, the findings discussed in this review underscore the promise of eco-friendly nanotechnology as a sustainable and effective platform for developing next-generation antiviral therapies against dengue virus.

papers.source_body_en: Dengue virus (DENV), a mosquito-borne pathogen belonging to the Flaviviridae family, continues to be a major global public health concern, causing millions of infections annually across tropical and subtropical regions. The virus encodes both structural and non-structural proteins that play critical roles in its replication, assembly, and immune evasion. Despite substantial research progress, there is still no specific antiviral drug available, and current treatment remains primarily supportive. This review highlights the significance of DENV structural proteins (C, prM/M, and E) and non-structural proteins (NS1–NS5) as potential molecular targets for antiviral interventions. Green-synthesized silver, gold, and iron oxide nanoparticles have demonstrated strong inhibitory activity against DENV by targeting key viral proteins such as the envelope (E), NS3 protease/helicase, and NS5 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. These nanoparticles interfere with viral entry, replication, and protein synthesis while exhibiting high biocompatibility and minimal cytotoxicity. Collectively, the findings discussed in this review underscore the promise of eco-friendly nanotechnology as a sustainable and effective platform for developing next-generation antiviral therapies against dengue virus.

papers.title: Predicting Dengue Clinical Severity in Eastern Sudan's 2023 Outbreak: A Comparative Analysis of Statistical and Machine Learning Models Using Routine Surveillance Data
papers.abstract: Objectives: This study characterized clinical severity patterns during the 2023 dengue outbreak in Al Qadarif State, Eastern Sudan; identified associated factors; compared statistical and machine-learning models; and explored patterns of clinical manifestations using routine surveillance data. Methods: This retrospective observational study included 2,552 dengue case records. The primary outcome was a pragmatic, study-specific composite clinical severity indicator, defined as the documented presence of bleeding, severe bleeding, loss of consciousness, convulsions, or thrombocytopenia.Analyses included descriptive statistics, multivariable logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, multiple correspondence analysis, and hierarchical clustering. Model performance was assessed using a stratified hold-out test set, with uncertainty estimated from 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Results: Overall, 182 patients (7.13%) met the study-specific composite clinical severity indicator.Thirty-two deaths were recorded, giving a case-fatality rate of 1.25%. Mortality was higher among patients with severity markers than among those without them (3.85% vs. 1.05%; relative risk=3.65). Skin rash showed the strongest adjusted association with the composite severity indicator (adjusted OR=6.26, 95% CI: 3.15–12.45; P<0.001), followed by symptom-onset timing (adjusted OR=4.65, 95% CI: 2.41–8.98; P<0.001). XGBoost achieved the numerically highest AUROC (0.765, 95% CI: 0.691–0.837) and the lowest Brier score (0.161, 95% CI: 0.145–0.176). Multiple correspondence analysis suggested hemorrhagic and neurological/systemic symptom patterns. Conclusion: The study-specific composite clinical severity indicator was uncommon but was associated with a higher risk of death. Skin rash and symptom-onset timing showed the strongest adjusted associations with the study-specific composite clinical severity indicator. Predictive performance was moderate, and the findings require confirmation using independent datasets with more detailed clinical and laboratory information.

analysis.methods: The study used routine surveillance data to define a pragmatic, study-specific composite clinical severity indicator. Analyses included descriptive statistics, multivariable logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, multiple correspondence analysis, and hierarchical clustering.
analysis.main_results: Overall, 182 patients (7.13%) met the study-specific composite clinical severity indicator. Thirty-two deaths were recorded, giving a case-fatality rate of 1.25%. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study-specific composite clinical severity indicator was uncommon but was associated with a higher risk of death. Skin rash and symptom-onset timing showed the strongest adjusted associations with the composite severity indicator.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more accurate clinical severity indicators and improve risk assessment for dengue patients in Eastern Sudan. They also highlight the importance of monitoring specific clinical markers for early identification of severe cases.

It aimed to identify factors associated with severe dengue and compare statistical and machine learning models for predictive performance. The study included 2,552 case records and defined a composite severity indicator based on documented clinical features. Results showed that 7.13% of patients met the severity criteria, with a case-fatality rate of 1.25%. Mortality was higher among patients with severity markers, and skin rash and symptom-onset timing were strongly associated with severity. XGBoost demonstrated the highest AUROC and lowest Brier score among the models tested. The study concluded that the findings require validation with more detailed clinical and laboratory data to improve predictive accuracy and risk assessment for dengue patients.

papers.title_zh: 预测东部苏丹2023年登革热临床严重程度:使用常规数据对统计模型和机器学习模型的比较分析
papers.source_body_en: Objectives: This study characterized clinical severity patterns during the 2023 dengue outbreak in Al Qadarif State, Eastern Sudan; identified associated factors; compared statistical and machine-learning models; and explored patterns of clinical manifestations using routine surveillance data. Methods: This retrospective observational study included 2,552 dengue case records. The primary outcome was a pragmatic, study-specific composite clinical severity indicator, defined as the documented presence of bleeding, severe bleeding, loss of consciousness, convulsions, or thrombocytopenia.Analyses included descriptive statistics, multivariable logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, multiple correspondence analysis, and hierarchical clustering. Model performance was assessed using a stratified hold-out test set, with uncertainty estimated from 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Results: Overall, 182 patients (7.13%) met the study-specific composite clinical severity indicator.Thirty-two deaths were recorded, giving a case-fatality rate of 1.25%. Mortality was higher among patients with severity markers than among those without them (3.85% vs. 1.05%; relative risk=3.65). Skin rash showed the strongest adjusted association with the composite severity indicator (adjusted OR=6.26, 95% CI: 3.15–12.45; P<0.001), followed by symptom-onset timing (adjusted OR=4.65, 95% CI: 2.41–8.98; P<0.001). XGBoost achieved the numerically highest AUROC (0.765, 95% CI: 0.691–0.837) and the lowest Brier score (0.161, 95% CI: 0.145–0.176). Multiple correspondence analysis suggested hemorrhagic and neurological/systemic symptom patterns. Conclusion: The study-specific composite clinical severity indicator was uncommon but was associated with a higher risk of death. Skin rash and symptom-onset timing showed the strongest adjusted associations with the study-specific composite clinical severity indicator. Predictive performance was moderate, and the findings require confirmation using independent datasets with more detailed clinical and laboratory information.

papers.title: Local thermal anomalies and the altitudinal rise of dengue hospitalisation rates in Ecuador, 2011–2024: a national ecological study
papers.abstract: Introduction Dengue is expanding beyond its traditional lowland range as rising temperatures may enable Aedes aegypti establishment at progressively higher altitudes. Ecuador, spanning sea level to above 4500 m, offers a natural altitudinal experiment, yet hospital-based evidence on the thermal drivers of Andean dengue is lacking. Methods We conducted a national ecological time-series analysis at the canton level using Ecuador's hospital discharge registry (INEC) for 2011–2024, the period with standardised canton coding, identifying dengue hospitalisations by ICD-10 codes A90, A91 and A97. Monthly land surface temperature, precipitation and vegetation index were derived from MODIS and GPM products. A distributed lag non-linear model estimated the temperature–hospitalisation association; a quasi-Poisson model restricted to Andean cantons (≥1500 m), with canton, calendar-month and year fixed effects, tested whether thermal anomalies above each canton's 2007–2015 baseline were associated with hospitalisation rates. Results Among 74,601 dengue hospitalisations with a resolvable canton of residence (232 deaths; case fatality 0.31%), dengue was recorded in 68 cantons above 1500 m, including altitudes exceeding 3000 m. The national hospitalisation rate rose from 29.7 to 77.0 per 100,000 and the Andean rate approximately 7-fold (1.9 to 12.8). The minimum hospitalisation temperature was 18.4°C nationally and 18.9°C in Andean cantons. A +1°C anomaly versus zero was associated with a 1.07-fold increase in hospitalisation rates (95% CI 1.02–1.13; p = 0.012). Without canton fixed effects, the same contrast yielded 1.21 (1.07–1.36); the within-canton association fell to 1.04 (1.00–1.08) when the 2024 epidemic year was excluded. Discussion Positive deviations from local historical baselines, rather than absolute temperature, were associated with rising dengue hospitalisation rates among Andean residents, by a modest margin that depends materially on the 2023–2024 epidemic. In-hospital case fatality was nearly twice as high in low Andean cantons (0.62%, 95% CI 0.20–1.45; five deaths) as on the coast (0.33%), a non-significant difference that nonetheless supports strengthening dengue recognition in highland facilities.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue is expanding beyond its traditional lowland range as rising temperatures may enable Aedes aegypti establishment at progressively higher altitudes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Ecuador, spanning sea level to above 4500 m, offers a natural altitudinal experiment, yet hospital-based evidence on the thermal drivers of Andean dengue is lacking.
analysis.methods: We conducted a national ecological time-series analysis at the canton level using Ecuador's hospital discharge registry (INEC) for 2011–2024, the period with standardised canton coding, identifying dengue hospitalisations by ICD-10 codes A90, A91 and A97.
analysis.main_results: Among 74,601 dengue hospitalisations with a resolvable canton of residence (232 deaths; case fatality 0.31%), dengue was recorded in 68 cantons above 1500 m, including altitudes exceeding 3000 m.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Positive deviations from local historical baselines, rather than absolute temperature, were associated with rising dengue hospitalisation rates among Andean residents, by a modest margin that depends materially on the 2023–2024 epidemic.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support strengthening dengue recognition in highland facilities and suggest that local thermal anomalies may influence dengue hospitalisation rates in higher altitude regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The national hospitalisation rate rose from 29.7 to 77.0 per 100,000 and the Andean rate approximately 7-fold (1.9 to 12.8).

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the relationship between local thermal anomalies and the altitudinal rise of dengue hospitalisation rates in Ecuador from 2011 to 2024. It highlights the expansion of dengue beyond traditional lowland areas and the potential influence of temperature changes on hospitalisation rates in higher altitude regions. The research utilises a national ecological time-series analysis of hospital discharge data, identifying dengue cases through ICD-10 codes. Results show that dengue hospitalisations occurred in cantons above 1500 m, with a significant increase in rates associated with temperature anomalies. The study suggests that local thermal variations, rather than absolute temperatures, may drive dengue hospitalisations in the Andes, particularly during the 2023–2024 epidemic. These findings have implications for improving dengue surveillance and recognition in highland facilities, but the study's ecological design and potential confounding factors limit the strength of the conclusions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 随着气温升高,登革热正在超出其传统的低地范围,可能使Aedes aegypti在更高海拔地区建立种群。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 厄瓜多尔海拔超过 4500 米,提供了自然海拔实验,但缺乏基于医院的关于安第斯登革热热驱动因素的证据。
elements_zh.methods: 我们使用厄瓜多尔医院出院登记系统(INEC)对2011–2024年期间(标准化的市镇编码时期)进行了全国生态学时间序列分析,按市镇级别进行,通过ICD-10代码A90、A91和A97识别登革热住院病例。
elements_zh.main_results: 在居住州可解决的 74,601 例登革热住院病例中(死亡 232 例,病死率 0.31%),其中 68 个州海拔 1500 m 以上,其中海拔超过 3000 m。

papers.title_zh: 厄瓜多尔2011–2024年登革热住院率海拔上升与局部热异常:一项全国生态学研究
papers.source_body_en: Introduction Dengue is expanding beyond its traditional lowland range as rising temperatures may enable Aedes aegypti establishment at progressively higher altitudes. Ecuador, spanning sea level to above 4500 m, offers a natural altitudinal experiment, yet hospital-based evidence on the thermal drivers of Andean dengue is lacking. Methods We conducted a national ecological time-series analysis at the canton level using Ecuador's hospital discharge registry (INEC) for 2011–2024, the period with standardised canton coding, identifying dengue hospitalisations by ICD-10 codes A90, A91 and A97. Monthly land surface temperature, precipitation and vegetation index were derived from MODIS and GPM products. A distributed lag non-linear model estimated the temperature–hospitalisation association; a quasi-Poisson model restricted to Andean cantons (≥1500 m), with canton, calendar-month and year fixed effects, tested whether thermal anomalies above each canton's 2007–2015 baseline were associated with hospitalisation rates. Results Among 74,601 dengue hospitalisations with a resolvable canton of residence (232 deaths; case fatality 0.31%), dengue was recorded in 68 cantons above 1500 m, including altitudes exceeding 3000 m. The national hospitalisation rate rose from 29.7 to 77.0 per 100,000 and the Andean rate approximately 7-fold (1.9 to 12.8). The minimum hospitalisation temperature was 18.4°C nationally and 18.9°C in Andean cantons. A +1°C anomaly versus zero was associated with a 1.07-fold increase in hospitalisation rates (95% CI 1.02–1.13; p = 0.012). Without canton fixed effects, the same contrast yielded 1.21 (1.07–1.36); the within-canton association fell to 1.04 (1.00–1.08) when the 2024 epidemic year was excluded. Discussion Positive deviations from local historical baselines, rather than absolute temperature, were associated with rising dengue hospitalisation rates among Andean residents, by a modest margin that depends materially on the 2023–2024 epidemic. In-hospital case fatality was nearly twice as high in low Andean cantons (0.62%, 95% CI 0.20–1.45; five deaths) as on the coast (0.33%), a non-significant difference that nonetheless supports strengthening dengue recognition in highland facilities.

papers.title: Neonatal Dengue Infection Mimicking Late-Onset Neonatal Sepsis in Endemic Regions: A Case Report Series and a Proposed Diagnostic Framework for Antimicrobial Stewardship
papers.abstract: Neonatal dengue infection may mimic late-onset neonatal sepsis (LOS) in endemic regions, leading to misdiagnosis and unnecessary antibiotic exposure. We describe a case series of neonates admitted to a tertiary referral hospital in a dengue-endemic area with suspected LOS who underwent standard sepsis evaluation, including blood cultures, inflammatory markers, and clinical assessment, and were subsequently tested for dengue infection by anti-dengue virus IgM using ELFA methodology on the VIDAS® platform. All patients presented with fever and hematologic abnormalities, particularly thrombocytopenia and/or leukopenia, while blood and urine cultures remained negative and procalcitonin levels were low or normal. Dengue IgM was positive in all cases, supporting the diagnosis of neonatal dengue infection. After diagnostic confirmation, antibiotics were discontinued when applicable, and all neonates had favorable clinical outcomes without complications at discharge. These findings highlight dengue as a potentially underrecognized differential diagnosis of LOS in endemic settings and suggest that arboviral testing may be considered in the diagnostic evaluation of neonates with suspected sepsis, particularly when cultures are negative and inflammatory markers are not suggestive of bacterial infection. Early recognition may help reduce unnecessary antimicrobial exposure and could support antimicrobial stewardship efforts.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a case series of neonates in a dengue-endemic region who exhibited symptoms resembling late-onset neonatal sepsis but were later diagnosed with neonatal dengue infection. The research aimed to highlight dengue as a potential differential diagnosis for neonatal sepsis, especially when standard diagnostic tests fail to identify bacterial causes. The study found that all neonates had positive dengue IgM results, indicating a clear diagnosis of dengue infection. The authors suggest that arboviral testing should be considered in neonates with suspected sepsis and negative cultures, to avoid unnecessary antibiotic use. The findings emphasize the importance of early recognition of dengue in neonates to support antimicrobial stewardship. The study is limited by its case series design, which may not capture broader trends, but the evidence is strong due to the clear diagnostic results and favorable clinical outcomes. The study contributes to the understanding of dengue in neonates and its implications for clinical practice in endemic areas.

elements_zh.main_results: 所有病例的登革热IgM均为阳性,支持新生儿登革热感染的诊断。

papers.source_body_en: Neonatal dengue infection may mimic late-onset neonatal sepsis (LOS) in endemic regions, leading to misdiagnosis and unnecessary antibiotic exposure. We describe a case series of neonates admitted to a tertiary referral hospital in a dengue-endemic area with suspected LOS who underwent standard sepsis evaluation, including blood cultures, inflammatory markers, and clinical assessment, and were subsequently tested for dengue infection by anti-dengue virus IgM using ELFA methodology on the VIDAS® platform. All patients presented with fever and hematologic abnormalities, particularly thrombocytopenia and/or leukopenia, while blood and urine cultures remained negative and procalcitonin levels were low or normal. Dengue IgM was positive in all cases, supporting the diagnosis of neonatal dengue infection. After diagnostic confirmation, antibiotics were discontinued when applicable, and all neonates had favorable clinical outcomes without complications at discharge. These findings highlight dengue as a potentially underrecognized differential diagnosis of LOS in endemic settings and suggest that arboviral testing may be considered in the diagnostic evaluation of neonates with suspected sepsis, particularly when cultures are negative and inflammatory markers are not suggestive of bacterial infection. Early recognition may help reduce unnecessary antimicrobial exposure and could support antimicrobial stewardship efforts.
papers.abstract_zh: 新生儿登革热感染可能在流行地区模拟晚发性新生儿脓毒症(LOS),导致误诊和不必要的抗生素暴露。我们描述了一组在登革热流行地区被收治于三级转诊医院的新生儿病例,这些新生儿疑似患有LOS,接受了标准的脓毒症评估,包括血液培养、炎症标志物和临床评估,并随后通过VIDAS®平台上的ELFA方法检测了抗-登革病毒 IgM以确定登革热感染。所有患者均表现为发热和血液学异常,特别是血小板减少和/或白细胞减少,而血液和尿液培养结果均为阴性,降钙素原水平低或正常。所有病例的登革热IgM均为阳性,支持新生儿登革热感染的诊断。在确诊后,当适用时停用抗生素,所有新生儿在出院时均表现出良好的临床结局,无并发症。这些发现强调登革热可能是流行地区LOS的一个被低估的鉴别诊断诊断,并建议在疑似脓毒症的新生儿中考虑进行虫媒病毒检测,尤其是在培养结果为阴性且炎症标志物不提示细菌感染的情况下。早期识别有助于减少不必要的抗菌药物暴露,并可能支持抗菌药物管理的努力。

papers.title: An Adaptive Gated Fusion-based Multimodal Framework for Influential Actor Identification in Dengue Haemorrhagic Fever Information Dissemination on YouTube
papers.abstract: Dengue hemorrhagic fever remains a critical public health concern in Indonesia, and YouTube has become a major channel for health information.Identifying influential actors is essential for public health communication, yet existing social network analysis relies on text and ignores visual signals such as video thumbnails.This study proposes a multimodal framework based on Adaptive Gated Fusion that combines text and visual features without any audio modality.Textual features from IndoBERT and visual features from ResNet-50 are fused adaptively per dimension, aggregated per channel, and used to build a content-based co-audience network analysed with PageRank.Using 33,233 Indonesian comments from 5,365 videos across 1,129 collected channels (1,084 retained after language filtering) over 2021 to 2025, an ablation study with stratified five-fold cross-validation shows the fused representation reaches 79.52 percent accuracy and 78.42 percent macro F1, outperforming text and visual baselines.KOMPASTV, Kata Dokter, and Halodoc emerged as the most influential actors.

papers.full_text: Received: June 18, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 668 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.34 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ An Adaptive Gated Fusion-based Multimodal Framework for Influential Actor Identification in Dengue Haemorrhagic Fever Information Dissemination on YouTube Ayu Eka Lestari1 Wiwik Anggraeni1* 1Department of Information Systems, Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember, Surabaya, Indonesia * Corresponding author’s Email: wiwik@is.its.ac.id Abstract: Dengue hemorrhagic fever remains a critical public health concern in Indonesia, and YouTube has become a major channel for health information. Identifying influential actors is essential for public health communication, yet existing social network analysis relies on text and ignores visual signals such as video thumbnails. This study proposes a multimodal framework based on Adaptive Gated Fusion that combines text and visual features without any audio modality. Textual features from IndoBERT and visual features from ResNet-50 are fused adaptively per dimension, aggregated per channel, and used to build a content-based co-audience network analysed with PageRank. Using 33,233 Indonesian comments from 5,365 videos across 1,129 collected channels (1,084 retained after language filtering) over 2021 to 2025, an ablation study with stratified five-fold cross-validation shows the fused representation reaches 79.52 percent accuracy and 78.42 percent macro F1, outperforming text and visual baselines. KOMPASTV, Kata Dokter, and Halodoc emerged as the most influential actors. Keywords: Adaptive gated fusion, Co-audience graph, Dengue haemorrhagic fever, IndoBERT, PageRank, ResNet- 50, Sentiment analysis, Social network analysis, YouTube. 1.
